transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, hello. I guess what finally scared me into making an appointment is... well, after I eat too much, I’ve been making myself throw up in the bathroom. I just do it so I won’t gain weight. But it’s gotten to the point where it isn’t just a one-time mistake anymore, and I knew I needed to talk to someone about it.
How often have you been making yourself throw up after eating?

Well, for at least the past several months, I'd say. It’s been happening most weeks now. I'll have one of those secret eating spells, and then I just go make myself sick right afterward. I really can’t honestly call it occasional anymore.
Can you describe what you mean by a 'secret eating spell'?

Well, it usually happens when I'm alone. Like, after a bridge night with my friends or when I get off a late shift at the store. I'll come home and... I just start eating. I might have leftover casserole, some cookies I baked, crackers, maybe a bowl of ice cream. And I eat it all in one sitting. It's... it's much more food than I would ever put on a plate if someone else was in the room with me.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yes, very much so. It really bothers me. If I'm getting ready for church and my skirt feels even a little tight, or if I catch a glimpse of my side view in one of the mirrors at the store... it honestly just ruins my whole day. I start feeling like everyone is looking at me and thinking I've completely let myself go. It's just a constant worry for me.
Do you think your weight is normal, even when you're at a weight that others might consider healthy?

Well, honestly, I don't really know what's normal for me anymore. People tell me I look fine, but... I just don't see it that way. Even if the scale says a number that's supposed to be okay for my height, I still feel heavy. I just can't seem to feel comfortable with it, no matter what anyone else thinks.
Do you see yourself as overweight when you look in the mirror, even if others say you are at a healthy weight?

I'm not really sure. I mean... I don't know if I look in the mirror and see someone who is completely overweight overall. I just see all the areas that bother me. 

Like, I'll focus right in on my stomach or my arms, and to me, they just look too big. I know what size clothes I buy for work, so I know I'm not huge, but... I just don't see the healthy person my friends say they see. I just see the parts of myself that I want to fix. So I guess I don't really know how to answer that, other than I just never like what I see.
When you look at yourself, do you think your body shape or weight is the way you actually see it in the mirror?
I guess I don't really know. I mean, I see what I see, but... I don't know if it's the reality of how I actually look. I just know what I focus on, and that's what seems real to me.
Have you ever had episodes where you ate a large amount of food in a short time without making yourself throw up afterward?
No, not really. I mean, if I eat a lot like that, I always end up throwing it up. I don't just eat a bunch of food and leave it at that. I always feel like I have to get rid of it.
Have you ever eaten a large amount of food in a short time without making yourself throw up afterward?

I think you might have just asked me that, but no. Like I was saying, if I eat a huge amount of food all at once, I always make myself sick afterward. I never just eat like that and keep it down. I always have to get rid of it.
Do you think you would still make yourself throw up after eating if you didn't fear gaining weight?

I don't really know. I mean... probably not? The whole reason I do it is because I'm so scared of putting on weight. I guess if I didn't have that fear, I wouldn't feel the need to get rid of the food. But it's hard to even imagine not worrying about it, to be honest.
Would you still feel the need to make yourself throw up after eating if you knew you wouldn't gain any weight from it?

I think you just asked me that, doctor. But, um... no, my answer is the same. If I knew for an absolute fact that I wouldn't gain any weight from the food, I wouldn't make myself sick. Keeping the weight off is really the only reason I do it.
Do you feel like you're in control when you're eating during these secret eating spells?

No, not really. Once I start during those times, it just... it feels like I'm on automatic. I'll be sitting there thinking I really should stop before my husband notices, but I just keep reaching for one more thing. I can't seem to stop myself once I get going.
Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you make yourself throw up after eating?

Yes, it is. I know we just went over this a minute ago, but yes, that's exactly it. That fear is the whole reason I do it. If I wasn't so worried about the scale going up, I wouldn't be making myself sick. It really just comes down to the weight.
Have you ever had an episode where you ate a large amount of food in a short time and didn't make yourself throw up afterward?

No, I don't think I ever have. If I have one of those spells where I eat a whole lot of food really fast, I always make myself sick afterward. I just... I couldn't stand to let all that sit in my stomach. So, no, I always do it.
Do you think your perception of your body shape is distorted?

I'm not sure if distorted is the right word, but it definitely takes over my thoughts. Like... if my skirt feels even a little tight before church, or if I happen to catch my side view in one of the mirrors at the store, it can just ruin my whole day. I immediately start feeling like everyone around me can tell I’ve let myself go. So, yes, how my shape looks is something I focus on a great deal.
Do you think your body shape is actually the way you see it?

I honestly don't know. I mean... when I look in the mirror, I see what I see, and it feels completely real to me. But I suppose... I'm just not sure if that's how I actually look to everyone else. It's hard to tell what the reality is when you worry about it as much as I do. So, I really couldn't say for sure.
Do you think your body shape is the same as how others see it?

Well, I guess... like I was just saying, I really don't know. I mean, I work the floor at the store all day, so I'm around people constantly, but... I have no idea if they see the same thing I see in the mirror. I just can't really tell what they're thinking when they look at me.
Do you think your body shape is distorted compared to how others see you?

I really couldn't tell you. Like I said, I just don't know if what I'm seeing is what everyone else is seeing. I don't know if my view is distorted or if it's the truth. I just know what I see when I look at myself, and I don't know how that compares to anyone else's view.
Have you ever eaten a large amount of food in a short time without trying to get rid of it afterward?

No, I... I don't think so. If I end up eating a whole lot of food all at once like that, I always feel like I have to get rid of it afterward. I don't think there's ever been a time where I just left it alone and didn't try to do something about it.
Do you think your body shape is distorted compared to a realistic and healthy body shape?

I don't really know how to answer that either. I just... I know what I look like to me, and I know I don't like it. But as far as what's realistic or healthy, or if my view is distorted from that... I honestly couldn't say. I just know what I see.
